lines.say: Why can an unseen watcher stop a yawn?
Many think yawning is contagious or boredom, just a mouth habit with no brain purpose.
That story starts to crack when you look closer.
Look first at the act itself: a deep breath in, on purpose, mouth stretched wide.
The command starts in the hypothalamus, then travels through the brainstem down to the spinal cord.
Chemical messengers like dopamine, serotonin and oxytocin help steer it, along with particular nerve pathways.
Newborns' brain and eye area cooled 0.36°C within 10 to 20 seconds of yawning.
Scientists haven't found that a yawn means you need sleep, or that low oxygen causes it.
When your jaw stretches wide, warm blood slips out of the skull and cools the brain.
Yawning likely cools the brain, as a wide jaw and altered breathing boost facial circulation.
Next time yawning hits, you'll know what your head is doing.
